A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPT-Agent research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–I are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original single-agent Overcooked experiments, evaluations with rule-based partners, and a human study with 71 recruited and 68 retained participants.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experiments and human-study outcomes and reports additional model comparisons in Table 1 and Appendices F–H.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same FSM, code-as-policy generator, Theory of Mind module, asynchronous reflection, and action executor. The corresponding implementation prompts in Appendices B–D are unchanged apart from editorial corrections.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Overcooked layouts, single-agent task, three specialized rule-based partners, and university-student population. Additional language models and reasoning configurations do not introduce new task or population coverage.

E2.justification: QwQ-32B joins the independent-agent and framework comparisons, and additional reasoning-model instantiations of ReAct and Reflexion appear in Tables 1 and 7–10. The underlying FSM, ReAct, and Reflexion comparator families and their implementations remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation configurations expand to include o3-mini medium/high reasoning levels, additional DeepSeek-R1 sizes, and QwQ-32B. Existing task timing, metrics, prompts, and human-study procedures remain unchanged. These are additional configurations, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 1 extends the existing ToM ablation to additional reasoning configurations. For example, o3-mini-high favors DPT-Agent without ToM, while DeepSeek-R1-671B favors the full agent, adding evidence about model-dependent ToM benefits. The human ablation and Appendix H.3 case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state 20 runs and reporting through inter-quartile means and standard errors. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear. Additional uncertainty-bearing rows and revised error values do not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 6–10 substantially expand results for reasoning models, including o3-mini-high scores of -43.00 with ReAct versus 55.17 with full DPT-Agent. Existing values also change: Qwen2.5-72B's full-agent score in Table 1 changes from 32.08 to 33.67, and Table 8 changes Mistral-nemo's missed/wrong-serve counts from 0/4 to 4/0. Overall averages now cover a different model set and are not same-setting performance gains. Human-study results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The DEC-MDP formulation, module equations, System 1/System 2 policy formulations, and Appendix E metric definitions are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The central claims about balancing latency and capability, autonomous simultaneous collaboration, and framework novelty retain their scope. The new abstract and introduction emphasis on translating slow reasoning into executable actions restates claims already made in v1 Sections 4.2.1 and 6.1.

C2.justification: v5 applies the existing reasoning-to-action explanation to the additional o3-mini and DeepSeek-R1 results without introducing a new mechanism explanation. Interpretations of variable ToM benefits and limitations concerning invalid policies, FSM flexibility, reasoning latency, and student-only sampling remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds a pointer to maintained evaluation results on AGI-Eval and shows the game and ranking-questionnaire interface in Figure 8. Existing code access, prompts, hardware, deployment descriptions, and cost disclosures are largely retained; the model inventories are not fully updated to match the expanded tables.

R1.justification: The generic OpenAI homepage reference is replaced by a dated GPT-4o mini release reference. This is a limited source replacement; the related-work discussion and positioning relative to DPT, ToM, and collaborative-agent research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 adds short passages emphasizing reasoning-model benefits, an acknowledgments section, and author contact information, and corrects several wording and spelling errors. The main narrative, section organization, and appendix structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 5 add QwQ-32B points, existing result tables expand and regroup model rows, and Figure 8 newly displays the experimental interface. Some table placement changes with text reflow. The architecture diagrams, task illustrations, and consent-form figure are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional reasoning-model results strengthen evidence that DPT-Agent remains useful under long inference delays, and Figure 8 makes the human-study interface inspectable. These are useful extensions of an already established empirical case. Documentation does not fully keep pace: Section 5.2 still describes 11 models although Table 1 reports 17 configurations. With the method, task coverage, and human-study evidence unchanged, the net improvement is limited.
